content:
If you've been testing Apple Watch app betas all summer, you may have noticed some existing apps failing to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is pushing automatic updates on behalf of developers.

The updates are rolling out via the App Store, with release notes reading: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features were added."

Apple informed developers earlier this week that the entire update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, iOS 27, and the other new operating systems are expected to roll out to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates should be wrapped up before the public launch.

Apple explained that because some watchOS apps were experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture, the measures were necessary. Reports indicate Apple is automatically reprocessing and repackaging affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue working without additional action from developers.
